summary: The note describes how Arab states emerged on the Arabian Peninsula during the partition of the Ottoman Empire. It covers Hussein bin Ali's Kingdom of Hejaz (1916), the Emirate of Riyadh becoming the Sultanate of Nejd, and the later formation of the Kingdom of Nejd and Hejaz (1926) and Saudi Arabia (1932). It also notes Yemen's independence in 1918 and the Persian Gulf Arab states becoming de facto British protectorates.
one_line: Overview of the Arab states that emerged on the Arabian Peninsula during the partition of the Ottoman Empire, 1916-1932.
key_facts: On the Arabian Peninsula, the Arabs were able to establish a number of independent states.
Hussein bin Ali, Sharif of Mecca, established the Kingdom of Hejaz in 1916.
In 1916 the Emirate of Riyadh was transformed into the Sultanate of Nejd.
In 1926 the Kingdom of Nejd and Hejaz was formed.
In 1932 the Kingdom of Nejd and Hejaz became the kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
The Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen became independent in 1918.
The Arab States of the Persian Gulf became de facto British protectorates.
The Arab States of the Persian Gulf retained some internal autonomy under British protectorate status.
